chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan ibn Yahya from 'Abdullah ibn Bukayr said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) married 'Ali (peace be upon him) to Fatimah (peace be upon her) with a dowry of a Kutami armor plate, which was worth thirty dirhams.'

key_terms.ثَلاَثِينَ دِرْهَماً: Thirty dirhams, the specified value of the dowry
key_terms.دِرْعٍ حُطَمِيَّةٍ: A type of armor plate from the Banu Kutam tribe, used here as the dowry

ai.seo_question: What was the dowry given to Fatimah (peace be upon her) upon her marriage to Ali (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the profound humility of the Ahl al-Bayt by specifying that the Prophet Muhammad arranged the marriage of Imam Ali and Fatimah with a dowry of a simple Kutami armor plate valued at thirty dirhams. This detail underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on *zuhd* (asceticism) and the rejection of material ostentation, illustrating that spiritual worth, rather than wealth, defined the status of the Prophet's household. The use of a functional military item as dowry further connects their domestic life to their role as leaders and defenders of the faith.
